newsitem.title: UK: Guernsey looks to build non-retail fund business.
newsitem.headline: Guernsey looks to build non-retail fund business.

text.p: Guernsey fund managers are looking to capitalise on emerging market interest by providing niche services to professional investors as competition in the industry hots up.
Fund managers on the island told Reuters many providers were looking to build non-retail fund business as they were less labour intensive and a more appropriate use of local expertise.

"Institutional funds are developing into a good future for Guernsey because investors can spread their risk across a number of different professional schemes and not be tied by retail fund rules," Peter Heaps, managing director of Management International (Guernsey) said.
At the end of 1996, Guernsey had 136 Class B open-ended funds and 161 closed-end funds against 40 Class A funds.
Class B funds offer more flexibility than the stricter rules covering Class A funds -- the equivalent of UK unit trusts.

The industry has built its presence in the fund management business on its proximity to London while remaining outside of the EU, its strict laws governing confidentiality and regulation and being constitutionally divorced from international jurisdiction.
The island's fiscal independence, political stability and low taxation are also seen helping to grow the business.
Another growing market for the island is non-Guernsey Schemes, where third party administration or custody of funds registered elsewhere is provided.

The schemes now account for three billion sterling of funds, with nine billion in open-ended and over four billion in closed-end funds. Of the open-ended fund investment, 3.2 billion sterling is in Class A schemes.

"At present Class A funds are a much larger part of local business, but non-retail class B funds have been our biggest growth area in the last five years," said Nick McCathie, managing director of Guinness Flight Fund Managers (Guernsey).
But he said Class A funds would continue to play a major part in Guernsey's fund business sector.
"It is very much a question of ensuring we keep pace with emerging developments globally, but preferably that we keep one step ahead of the competition."
